extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, program managers, policymakers, Congress, and external IP stakeholders (practitioners, registrants, public)
extracted.subtask_description: Performance and accountability criteria and operational standards used to evaluate and manage the USPTO's patent (and related trademark/IP) business lines, including strategic objectives, revenue/fee rules, operational controls, and audit-driven corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize patent quality and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic priority to optimize patent quality and timeliness (part of USPTO strategic priorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This priority appears in the agency strategic framework and is operationalized via objectives such as optimizing application pendency and issuing highly reliable patents. Performance measures and management attention focus on pendency, first action pendency, examination quality, and timeliness of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize trademark quality and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic priority to optimize trademark quality and timeliness (part of USPTO strategic priorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding objectives include optimizing trademark application pendency and issuing high-quality trademarks. Measures include application filings, registrations issued, disposals, and timeliness metrics tied to fee rates and staff resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide domestic and global leadership on IP policy, enforcement, and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic priority to provide domestic and global leadership to improve intellectual property policy, enforcement, and protection worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses leadership, education, and engagement on domestic and international IP policy and awareness; measured through program activities and costs in the IP Policy, Protection, and EnforcementWorldwide program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission support goal: deliver organizational excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission support goal to deliver organizational excellence across USPTO operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers organizational performance areas such as earned revenue management, program costs, IT modernization, procurement, and internal controls that support the patent and trademark business lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize patent and trademark application pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: optimizing patent and trademark application pendency as part of the strategic performance framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via pendency metrics (e.g., first action pendency, total pendency) and managed through staffing, process improvements, and IT systems to meet strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue highly reliable patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to issue highly reliable patents (reliability/quality of issued patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assessed by internal quality review programs, PTAB/PTAB interactions, error rates, and audits; reliability is a complement to timeliness in performance evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue high-quality trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to issue high-quality trademarks (accuracy and integrity of the trademark register).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality measured through trademark examination controls, post-registration maintenance, and TTAB effectiveness; concerns include preventing fraudulent or inaccurate registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster business effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to foster business effectiveness across USPTO business lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes improving operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, resource allocation, and achieving targets for revenue collection versus costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance operations of the PTAB and TTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to enhance the operations of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) and Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers IT systems, case management, data governance, staffing projections, and process improvements identified in audits and corrective action plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide leadership and education on domestic and international IP policy and awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to provide leadership and education for IP policy and awareness domestically and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities and programs tracked under IP Policy, Protection, and Enforcement Worldwide efforts; measured by program outputs and engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance human capital management and foster employee engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to improve human capital management and employee engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via workforce metrics (staffing levels, recruitment/retention impacts from decisions like Arthrex), training, and programs to sustain capacity and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize speed, quality, and cost-effectiveness of IT delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to optimize the speed, quality, and cost-effectiveness of IT delivery (OCIO/IT modernization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes replacing legacy systems, reducing IT contractual services costs, improving system reliability/resilience, and aligning delivery practices (e.g., New Ways of Working). OIG audit findings and corrective actions (e.g., SDI-NG procurement) feed into this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure financial stability for effective operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to ensure financial stability for USPTO operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses fee collection strategies, operating reserves, PTFRF deposits, budgetary resource management, and fee schedule design to recover aggregate operating costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance interactions with internal and external stakeholders and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to enhance interactions with stakeholders and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes transparency of performance reporting, stakeholder outreach, and mechanisms to solicit and respond to public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent maintenance fee payment rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees are due at 3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years after issue; payments during a six-month 'window period' prior to each due date; six-month 'grace period' after due date with surcharge; unpaid fees cause lapse and require petition and proper fees for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural requirements affect patent validity and enforcement and materially impact USPTO earned revenue timing. The window enables advance payment ahead of fee changes; late payments require surcharge and potentially a petition to reinstate rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and revenue treatment of maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees are recognized immediately as earned revenue at the time of payment; timing and rate changes can materially affect USPTO earned revenue across fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report uses earned revenue accounting to explain shifts in revenue when customers prepay maintenance fees before fee increases. Forecasting must account for payment timing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring patent renewal rates and drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO monitors first-, second-, and third-stage patent renewal (maintenance) rates by issue year and analyzes drivers such as court decisions, IP budgets, perceived patent value, fee rates, and the economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal rates are used for forecasting maintenance fee revenue; preliminary data caveats apply (e.g., windows/grace periods); trends are tracked and updated as additional payments arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fee structure and principal revenue components
rubrics_metrics.description: Major components of earned patent revenue are maintenance fees; initial application fees for filing, search, and examination; and issue fees (together comprising approximately 85.6% of total patent income).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the composition of fee revenue informs budgeting and fee-setting decisions and highlights the relative importance of maintenance fees to USPTO finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee schedule review and adjustment process
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO conducts patent and trademark biennial fee reviews; the process to review, analyze, and set fees typically takes at least two years and is designed to recover aggregate operating costs while achieving financial and operational targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-setting requires long lead times and considers operational targets, cost recovery, and stakeholder impacts; biennial reviews and potential rulemaking are part of this rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve acquisition planning and vendor performance management (OIG findings/corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion to improve acquisition planning and vendor performance management to prevent schedule delays and unnecessary costs (OIG OIG-21-010-A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned and taken actions include: restrict period of performance for orders to no more than 12 months after base IDV expiration; create an Acquisition Team for strategy/timeline/risk mitigation; document past performance prior to option exercise; develop a vendor performance evaluation dashboard to aggregate vendor performance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB operational, IT, and data management improvements (OIG findings/corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion to address PTAB deficiencies in end-to-end IT system fit, data management, staffing projection capabilities, and the impacts of Arthrex (OIG-21-025-I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned corrective actions include creating a Lead Product Owner reporting to a PTAB senior executive; evaluating data quality and governance programs; coordinating with OCIO to identify requirements for alternative case management; address staffing and retention issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA and PTE calculation controls and SOPs (OIG findings/corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO should improve internal controls and oversight related to Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) and Patent Term Extension (PTE) calculations (OIG-21-030-I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned actions: publish proposed rulemaking regarding use of safe-harbor form PTO/SB/134 for 37 CFR § 1.704(d) exceptions; create PTA-PTE SOPs covering events that necessitate updates to PTA calculator software; study e-filing acceptance for PTEs; feasibility study for workflow tools for Legal Instrument Examiners; determine sample size and method for statistically valid random PTA calculation reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls to improve trademark examination integrity (OIG findings/corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO should improve controls over examination of trademark filings to enhance integrity of the trademark register (OIG-21-033-A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned/candidate corrective actions include: implement automated queries to flag PO boxes and 'care of' addresses; draft SOPs to identify suspicious attorney activity and evidence for referral to Office of Enrollment and Discipline; form a working group to improve specimen examination; use Admin Console to quarantine suspicious application groups pre-exam; provide guidance on what constitutes a 'wide' range of unrelated goods under section 904.01(a); document Trademarks' risk framework (ERM Scorecard); modify OTQRT database to allow manager input directly into quality review workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance audits and corrective action tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO responds to OIG and audit recommendations with corrective actions; management concurs with recommendations and tracks planned actions until closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR documents specific OIG reports, numbers of recommendations, and planned actions (e.g., updates to procurement policies, Tiger Team for acquisition documentation). Audit outcomes and follow-ups are part of the agency's performance accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance data verification and validation: accountability for data quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers of USPTO programs are responsible and accountable for ensuring performance data is accurate, complete, and reliable per GPRA Modernization Act requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO has developed strategies for validating and verifying performance results; program managers must ensure procedures exist to maintain data quality and credibility for reported performance measures.
